summary: Ramesh Chandra Majumdar was an Indian historian and Indologist who studied at institutions including Ravenshaw, Presidency, and Calcutta universities. He held posts at the University of Calcutta (~1914–1921), the University of Chicago (~1958), and chaired the History of Bengal Publication Committee.

Ramesh Shankar Gupte was an Indologist and historian. In 1967, he was Head of History & Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest University, Salem College, and Winston-Salem State University.
Ramin Etesami is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015) under the supervision of Lobsang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina.

Ramkrishna Gopal Bhandarkar (1837–1925) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Martin Haug and at Elphinstone College, University of Mumbai, and University of Göttingen. He was a professor at Deccan College (~1882–1893) and Elphinstone College (attested 1907).
Ramón Prats is a Tibetologist who held positions at Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources (attested 1999) and Pompeu Fabra University (attested 2017).
Randall Studstill is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied under doctoral supervisor Richard K. Payne and teacher Steven D. Goodman.

Rangama Chandawimala is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliye Anuruddha, having also studied under traditional teacher Attaragama Gnanawimala.

Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (1924–1981) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master who studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Kalu Rinpoche, Tai Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, and Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, teaching numerous prominent figures.
Raniero Gnoli (1930–2025) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He held a post at Sapienza University of Rome from approximately 1964 to 2000.
Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who served as a professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested 2003, 2017).

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh (1897–1982) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Fergusson College and under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He served as Professor at Gujarat Vidyapith (~1920–1940) and as Secretary of Gujarat Puratattva Mandir.
Rasmus Rask (1787–1832) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1807–1812). He later served there as Professor of Literary History and Librarian (~1825–1832).

Ravindra Singh Bisht (b. 1944) is an Indian archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Lucknow. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1999–2004).
Rawi Bhavilai (1925–2017) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Adelaide (~1956–1961). He served as a Director at Chulalongkorn University (attested 2002).

Rebecca Redwood French is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Washington and Yale University under mentors including Stanley Weinstein and Robert Thurman, she held law faculty posts at Colorado Boulder and University at Buffalo.

Regbi Pubaev (1928–1991) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St. Petersburg University. He worked at the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies (~1958–1991) and Buryat State University.

Reginald A. Ray (b. 1942) is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. Trained under Mircea Eliade, Chögyam Trungpa, and others, he held posts at Naropa University (attested 2001–2006) and the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 2001–2002).
Rei Yoshimura (1929–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University (~1949–1953) and later served there as a professor from approximately 1972 to 2000.

Reiko Ohnuma (b. 1964) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at UC Berkeley and the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, she held posts at UT Austin, University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College.

Reimon Yuki (1902–1992) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1927). He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1963) and held posts at Kyoto Women's and Ryukoku universities.
